summary: Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710). Sidebar project/thread/worktree/chat lists and the inbox no longer observe or measure while they populate at boot. useSidebarListMotionReady keeps motion off until some environment has a live snapshot (bootstrapComplete), then turns it on one rAF later and latches. Cache-hydrated rows (primary shell cache, desktop workspace cache, hosted read cache) also populate with motion off, because hydration leaves bootstrapComplete false. While disabled, attachSidebarAutoAnimateNode never calls autoAnimate(). That matters: in auto-animate 0.10 a disabled controller still calls getCoords() in add()/remain() before its isEnabled check, so creating controllers and disabling them would not have been enough. useInboxListMotion skips every layout read when enabled is false. Its ResizeObserver stays attached but does no row reads while signatureRef is null. When motion turns on, the first read uses duration 0, so nothing flashes in. useFlipLayout's trigger effect now has [ref, trigger] deps and returns early when the trigger is unchanged. Resting positions come from a ResizeObserver and MutationObserver set up once per element, and a browser test (useFlipLayout.browser.tsx) checks that commits which leave the row alone call no getBoundingClientRect. Residual nits only, none of which undo the fix: (1) the latch fires on ANY environment's first live snapshot, as the proposal specified, so a second environment's population can still be animated and measured. With the per-environment caches this is mostly limited to cache/live differences. (2) After latching, the hook still subscribes to selectAnyShellSnapshotApplied, so Sidebar re-renders whenever all environments demote and recover. (3) Turning motion on changes the ref-callback identity, so the memoized sidebar subtree re-renders once, one frame after first paint. This only happens when the list is under the thresholds. (4) The hook has no unit test. Separate pre-existing issue, not part of this finding: pruned auto-animate controllers are never destroy()ed (Sidebar.tsx:167-175), so the library's 2-second per-child poll timers and IntersectionObservers keep running for detached lists.

evidence.note: Latch: true once any environment has bootstrapComplete, then setReady one requestAnimationFrame later (setTimeout fallback). Module-level motionReadyLatched keeps it on for the session.
bootstrapComplete is set to true only by the live shell snapshot apply path.
hydrateEnvironmentStateFromCache leaves bootstrapComplete false, so rows from the primaryShellCache, desktopWorkspace and hosted readCache paths populate with motion off.
shouldAnimateProjectLists and shouldAnimateThreadLists are gated by listMotionReady before shouldEnableAutoAnimate is applied.

No autoAnimate() call while disabled, so no MutationObserver, ResizeObserver or per-child getCoords exists during population. The ref callbacks (1073-1081, 1106-1114) change identity with enabled, and the memoized children (SidebarProjectList:570, SidebarProjectThreadList:234, SidebarWorktreeList:174, SidebarChatList:163) use default shallow memo, so they re-attach.
add() and remain() call getCoords() before checking isEnabled, so a disabled controller would still measure on mutations. Not creating the controller is the right approach.
motionReady={listMotionReady} is passed to ConnectedInboxSidebar, which spreads its props into InboxSidebar (ConnectedInboxSidebar.tsx:97-98).
When !input.enabled, the effect returns before getClientRects and offsetTop reads. When the inbox is first enabled, it reads with duration 0 because signatureRef is null, so nothing animates in.
Trigger effect deps are [ref, trigger] with an early return when Object.is says the trigger is unchanged. At f1be4abc7 it was dep-less and called recordResting on every commit.
Observers are set up once per element. Positions are recorded on DOM mutations and resizes of the row, not on every commit.
Browser test: five rerenders that leave the row untouched call getBoundingClientRect and getAnimations zero times.
Only caller of useFlipLayout: the new-thread hero sentence, which has a handful of tokens.

Adjacent, pre-existing and out of scope: pruneDisconnectedSidebarAutoAnimateControllers drops controllers from the map without calling destroy(), so auto-animate's poll() intervals (index.mjs:174-177, cleared only by disable/destroy) keep running for children of detached lists.

fixDefects: No real defect in the fix. Minor nits: (a) useSidebarListMotionReady.ts:23 keeps the store subscription after latching, so Sidebar re-renders whenever every environment's bootstrapComplete flips false and back (disconnect, then reconnect). That is a negligible extra render during a reconnect. (b) The latch uses ANY environment's first live snapshot, so later environments still populate with motion on. Every boot path hydrates all environments from cache first, so in practice this mostly limits measurement to cache/live differences. (c) Turning motion on changes the ref-callback identity, which re-renders the memoized sidebar subtree once. This is bounded by the thresholds and happens after first paint. (d) There is no unit or browser test for useSidebarListMotionReady or for the sidebar's 'no autoAnimate before ready' behaviour.
implementationSketch: Optional polish only. (1) In useSidebarListMotionReady, select a constant once ready (e.g. useStore(ready ? selectTrue : selectAnyShellSnapshotApplied)) so later demote/recover flips do not re-render Sidebar. (2) Optionally gate on 'every environment known at boot is bootstrapped or 2s elapsed' instead of 'any environment', for multi-node first boots without a cache. This is a small UX trade-off, because late environments would then appear without an entrance fade. (3) Add a browser test: mount Sidebar with a store that has cache-hydrated rows, spy on Element.prototype.getBoundingClientRect, assert zero calls until syncServerShellSnapshot runs and a frame passes, then assert that a later row insertion animates. Separate follow-up, not this finding: call controller.destroy() for pruned controllers in pruneDisconnectedSidebarAutoAnimateControllers (Sidebar.tsx:167-175), or have the ref callback destroy on null via React 19 ref cleanup. That stops leaked 2-second auto-animate poll timers and IntersectionObservers for lists that were unmounted (collapsed projects, remounted panes).
decisionReason: No E2EE, auth, hosted-lifecycle or Hub change. The only product choice is the optional 'all environments ready' gate, which is cosmetic.
